hunt.justification: Threat actors are increasingly embedding AI and legitimate low-code automation into their kill chain to scale operations. Detecting these blunders and workflow anomalies is critical for preempting phishing campaigns.

meta.analysis: This is a hunt because these services (Make.com, Google Translate, Censys) are often legitimate. A single detection rule would be too noisy. The hunt pivots between domain resolution, fleet-wide rarity, and keyword-based web patterns to build a suspicious context an agent and analyst must weigh.

stages.name: Session Token Theft and Identity Abuse

scenario.summary: An attacker's operational security failure—installing a security agent on their own jump box—revealed a highly automated workflow using AI tools and Make.com for phishing and targeting. The actor specialized in credential theft through Evilginx instances and maintained long-term access to thousands of identities by refreshing session tokens and creating malicious mail rules.

meta.rationale: Start with general user workstations. Marketing or Sales departments may have a higher baseline for Make.com; focus initial analysis on rare instances in IT or Engineering segments.
meta.hypothesis: An attacker is using legitimate automation platforms and AI-writing assistants to generate localized phishing content and discover external infrastructure, visible through specific DNS and web telemetry patterns.

blind_spots.risk: Without inspection, we only see the domains. We cannot distinguish between a user asking ChatGPT for a recipe vs. an attacker generating phishing lure content.
blind_spots.question: What are the specific URL paths and payloads being sent to Make.com or AI assistants?
blind_spots.remediation: Deploy TLS break-and-inspect on corporate gateways for higher-risk egress.

blind_spots.risk: These would not appear in DNS queries for public domains like Make.com, bypassing the scoping query.
blind_spots.question: Is the attacker using self-hosted automation tools like n8n or local LLMs?
blind_spots.remediation: Include queries for common self-hosted automation tool ports and binary names.

hunt.name: Automated AI-Driven Phishing Reconnaissance
hunt.description: This hunt identifies hosts interacting with a specific set of automation (Make.com), AI generation (Toolbaz, DocsBot, Explo), and infrastructure discovery (Censys) services mentioned in recent research. It focuses on the 'automated-targeting-recon' and 'external-infrastructure-discovery' stages by looking for anomalous combinations of these tools, which indicate an attacker streamlining their reconnaissance and content generation workflows.

nodes.label: DNS resolution for recon and automation domains

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name, COUNT(*) as lookup_count, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{recon_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name
config.description: Identify hosts resolving domains used for AI content generation and infrastructure discovery.
config.expected_signal: Hosts resolving make.com, toolbaz.com, or censys.io. While some (like Make.com) may be legitimate, Toolbaz and DocsBot are less common in corporate environments.

primitive_config.label: DNS resolution for recon and automation domains
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name, COUNT(*) as lookup_count, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{recon_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name
primitive_config.expected: Hosts resolving make.com, toolbaz.com, or censys.io. While some (like Make.com) may be legitimate, Toolbaz and DocsBot are less common in corporate environments.

config.content: SELECT query_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) as host_count, MIN(time) as first_seen_in_window FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{recon_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY query_hostname HAVING host_count <= 5
config.description: Stack-count unique host associations with the recon domains to isolate outliers.
config.expected_signal: Domains like 'toolbaz.com' or 'docsbot.ai' appearing on only one or two hosts, whereas 'make.com' might appear across many.

primitive_config.label: Fleet-wide prevalence of recon domains
primitive_config.content: SELECT query_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) as host_count, MIN(time) as first_seen_in_window FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{recon_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY query_hostname HAVING host_count <= 5
primitive_config.expected: Domains like 'toolbaz.com' or 'docsbot.ai' appearing on only one or two hosts, whereas 'make.com' might appear across many.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, url_hostname, url_path, url_query, user_agent, time FROM hb_http_activity WHERE (LOWER(url_hostname) LIKE '%censys%' OR LOWER(url_path) LIKE '%translate%' OR LOWER(url_hostname) LIKE '%evilginx%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find web requests containing keywords like 'censys' or 'translate' that indicate manual or automated discovery.
config.expected_signal: HTTP requests to search engines or translation services involving 'Evilginx' or Censys search queries.

primitive_config.label: HTTP patterns matching recon activity

config.objective: Determine if any host is using the combination of Make.com, AI writing tools, and Censys for malicious reconnaissance or phishing content generation.
config.description: Correlate the DNS resolutions with rarity and HTTP patterns to identify suspicious activity.
config.expected_signal: A verdict on whether a host's activity matches the described attacker profile.
config.success_criteria: Categorize hosts as 'suspicious' if they use multiple rare tools from the list, particularly when combined with Censys searches.
